Subject: Post-demo: security questionnaire selection + SOC 2 / HIPAA overview

Hi Amanda —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for carving out time. Quick recap from our demo and a couple of clarification questions so we can get the security intake moving:

1) Questionnaire preference
   - We can complete a SIG-Lite prefill, a full CAIQ, or a short custom checklist mapped to your HIPAA+GDPR asks. Which format would you prefer for the initial intake? SIG-Lite is usually fastest for engineering-reviewed artifacts.

2) Compliance posture (quick bullets)
   - SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II coverage (scope: control plane and inference runtime; last assessment completed Jun 2026).
   - HIPAA: We support HIPAA workloads in Dedicated and Private deployments; can sign a BAA — we occasionally negotiate a few standard redlines.
   - GDPR: Data residency and DPA templates available; we support EU regions.

3) Specific asks from your side
   - Is HealthAlign looking for an executed BAA before we start the questionnaire, or is a signed BAA acceptable after we provide the initial SIG-Lite prefill?
   - Do you have a preferred KMS/keys requirement (e.g., CMEK)?
   - Target timeline: do you have an internal deadline for security sign-off?

I attached a one-pager and a short SOC 2 summary to help your team triage artifacts (product-security-onepager.pdf, SOC2-Summary-2026.pdf). If SIG-Lite is ok, we can deliver a prefill in ~7–10 business days assuming no unexpected evidence gaps. If you prefer CAIQ or a custom form, timelines will vary — I can provide an estimate once you confirm.

Next steps: 1) confirm preferred form (SIG-Lite/CAIQ/custom), 2) confirm timeline and whether Procurement wants an executed BAA up front, 3) point us to a security contact for evidence uploads (or we can upload to a secure Drive link).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow-up with your security team if helpful.

Best,

Thanks Avery — good session. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) Form preference: SIG-Lite is our preferred starting point for third-party vendors — lightweight and lets us move quickly. If SIG-Lite looks clean we may not request a full CAIQ.

2) BAA: We need an executed BAA before moving any PHI into a vendor environment. Can Redwood provide a standard BAA? If you typically require redlines, please flag any clauses we should expect to adjust.

3) KMS / encryption: We require encryption at rest with customer keying for production PHI workloads (CMEK preferred). Please confirm whether Redwood supports AWS KMS CMEK for Hosted/Dedicated and what options exist for Private or on-prem (HSM).

4) Evidence & timeline: Our initial review window is two weeks once we receive the SIG-Lite prefill and the BAA. Can you commit to delivering the prefill + minimal evidence within 10 business days of BAA agreement?

5) Contacts: I will loop in our InfoSec engineer (cc’d via procurement).

Appreciate the SOC 2 summary — that helps. Please include a short dataflow diagram that shows where PHI may touch Redwood systems and which hosting modes are permitted for PHI.

Regards,
Amanda Lee
Head of Information Security, HealthAlign
amanda.lee@healthalign.com

Avery — quick answers and an action checklist below. I can take point on the SIG-Lite prefill and BAA negotiation.

SOC 2
- Status: SOC 2 Type II report (period ending May 2026) covering control plane and inference runtime; independent auditor available for redaction requests.

BAA
- We can execute HealthAlign’s BAA; typical exceptions we flag: indemnity cap alignment and subprocessors notification window. We can often agree to a standard BAA with 2–3 minor redlines. Legal can turn around a reviewed BAA in ~3 business days once received.

KMS / CMEK
- Hosted API (multi-tenant hosted): we currently support envelope encryption; customer-provided CMEK is available on Redwood Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we can discuss a confederated CMEK approach via customer KMS for enterprise tiers — will require a short engineering engagement.
- Private / On-prem: full CMEK/HSM support (customer-managed).

Minimal evidence bundle for 10-business-day SIG-Lite prefill
1) SOC2 summary + auditor contact (attached: SOC2-Summary-2026.pdf)
2) Encryption & KMS note (summary paragraph)
3) Dataflow diagram (Grace to produce; we can attach PNG)
4) Access control & RBAC summary (1–2 paragraphs)
5) Incident response summary + last test date

I estimate the team can assemble the prefill and attachments in 7–10 business days once BAA is agreed and HealthAlign provides one point of contact for evidence upload. If Procurement insists on seeing a fully executed BAA immediately, Legal can prioritize that in parallel.

Action items (owners):

- Avery: confirm to Amanda that we can sign BAA (subject to minor redlines), propose 10-business-day prefill after BAA, and provide upload link.
- Sean: be ready to escalate to Legal if Procurement pushes nonstandard indemnity terms.
